hourly.summary: Arsenal fans are revelling in Manchester City's 115-charge guilty verdict with the schadenfreude of a north London derby win at the Emirates. The dominant mood is vindication—years of 'financial doping' accusations finally validated—mixed with giddy speculation about retroactive titles, Gyökeres joining the title push, and whether Haaland might fancy a move to a club that doesn't need 115 loopholes to compete. Even the away kit discount feels like a title parade.

daily.summary: Arsenal fan sentiment deteriorated across the day, shifting from early transfer apprehension and post-Brighton unease to a measured split between women's team optimism and men's concerns, before plunging into full injury-crisis panic after Havertz limped off on international duty. The women's side (Emily Fox extension, MLS composure) and youth breakthroughs provided the only consistent bright spots, while Arteta's new contract served as a fragile anchor amid mounting defensive absences and transfer window frustration.

weekly.summary: Arsenal fan sentiment traced a dramatic boom-and-bust arc across the week: cautious optimism early on built into bullish, title-chasing euphoria by mid-week, only to implode catastrophically after a 3-0 loss at Brighton on the 19th. The final two days saw sentiment plummet from peak confidence (8/10) to meltdown and despair (3/10), with Arteta's 'lack of respect' critique, exposed defensive frailties, and extinguished title hopes defining a thoroughly miserable finish.
